sections.h2: Where is Spartanburg County and what does it include?
sections.html:
Spartanburg County sits in the northwest corner of South Carolina against the North Carolina line. It covers 819.74 square miles, of which 808.34 are land, and it is bordered by Rutherford and Polk counties in North Carolina and by Cherokee, Union, Laurens and Greenville counties in South Carolina (Wikipedia).

The county is named for the Spartan Regiment, a local militia in the Revolutionary War, and the city of Spartanburg is both the seat and the largest community. Around it are Greer, Duncan, Boiling Springs, Inman, Landrum and Woodruff, so a house sale here can mean a downtown bungalow, a suburban subdivision near the interstate or a rural lot.

Property tax follows that variety. Two homes a few miles apart can sit in different school districts or municipalities and carry different millage, so always look up the exact parcel on the county's tax record rather than comparing neighbors.

sections.h2: What drives the Spartanburg County economy?
sections.html:
Manufacturing is the largest employment sector, at 24.1% in the third quarter of 2023, followed by health care and retail. County gross domestic product for 2022 was $19.5 billion.

The employer list on the county's Wikipedia page includes Adidas, BMW, Ingles, Michelin, Optum, QuikTrip, Sage Automotive Interiors, Siemens and Walmart. In the city of Spartanburg itself, the 2022 annual report ranks Spartanburg Regional first at 9,648 employees, then Spartanburg County government at 1,515 and Spartanburg School District 7 at 1,273. The BMW plant in nearby Greer had about 8,800 employees as of 2017.

Large employers explain why people move here and why some owners need to sell on short notice: a relocation, a transfer or an inherited house from a parent who worked at one of the mills. The mills themselves are history. About 40 textile mills operated around Spartanburg by the early 1900s, and production fell from the 1950s as jobs moved offshore.

sections.h2: How do roads, rail and the airport shape where buyers look?
sections.html:
Interstates 26, 85 and 585 cross the county, along with US 29, US 176 and US 221. Greenville-Spartanburg International Airport and the Inland Port Greer rail depot are also in the county.

Amtrak's Crescent line stops at 290 Magnolia Street in Spartanburg, and the SPARTA bus system runs eight routes from a passenger center at 100 North Liberty Street. The Daniel Morgan Trail System adds 55 miles of paved and unpaved trails, sidewalks and protected bike lanes.

Houses with quick access to I-85 or I-26 tend to draw commuters, and houses in older neighborhoods such as Hampton Heights, the Beaumont Mill village historic district or Glendale draw a different crowd. If your house is in a historic district, check with the city before planning exterior work.

sections.h2: What is the climate, and what does it mean for an older house?
sections.html:
Spartanburg has a humid subtropical climate with long, hot, humid summers and cool to semi-mild winters. Average annual temperature is about 61.6 degrees Fahrenheit, rainfall runs 50 to 51 inches a year and snow averages under two inches.

That mix is hard on crawl spaces and roofs. Moisture under a 1950s mill house, clogged gutters and aging shingles are the usual repair bills that make an owner consider selling as-is instead of fixing everything first.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Spartanburg County?
sections.html:
Three offices split the work: the Assessor sets value and handles appeals, the Auditor handles exemptions and the Treasurer and Delinquent Tax Office collect. The county's appeals page lists the Administration Building at 366 N Church Street, Spartanburg, open Monday through Friday from 8 AM to 5 PM, and gives no phone number for the Assessor.

The Delinquent Tax Office can be reached at 864-596-2597 or at P.O. Box 3060, Spartanburg, SC 29304.

sections.h2: When is Spartanburg County property tax due and what are the penalties?
sections.html:
Taxes are due between September 30 and January 15 after assessment. The county's tax sale procedures page lists the penalty steps, and S.C. Code 12-45-180 sets the same percentages in the state code.

If the bill is unpaid byPenalty addedRunning total
January 163%3%
February 2 (statute) or after February 1 (county page)7%10%
March 175%15%

After the March date the bill is delinquent and the Treasurer issues a tax execution to the Tax Collector. The statute lets the Treasurer waive penalties when a taxpayer shows clear and convincing evidence of timely payment, and requires a waiver in some cases where a title transfer left the owner without timely notice.

sections.h2: How does the 2023 reappraisal affect the bill?
sections.html:
Values were reset to market conditions as of December 31, 2022, and the 2023 bill was based on them. The county mailed more than 180,567 reappraisal notices by September 2023.

  • Increases from a reappraisal are limited to 15%, unless the property has new or improved structures, sold or had a transfer of interest.
  • The notice is not a tax bill, and tax notices were due January 16, 2024.
  • State law requires reappraisal every five years, and the county page does not give the next date, so ask the Assessor.

If you bought or sold recently, the 15% cap may not protect the new owner, which is why a buyer should estimate the bill from the new value rather than the seller's old one.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Spartanburg County assessment?
sections.html:
File a written objection within 90 days of the date the Assessor mails the notice. The county appeals page lays out the sequence.

  1. Request an Assessor meeting in writing. If the Assessor agrees, the change is made and the appeal ends.
  2. If not, attend the conference. Missing it waives further appeal for that year.
  3. File a written protest with your facts, legal reasons and claimed value.
  4. The Assessor answers in writing in about 30 days. You then have 30 days to appeal to the County Board of Assessment Appeals.
  5. Request a contested case before the Administrative Law Court within 30 days of the Board's decision.

In years without a reappraisal notice, an appeal filed before January 15 applies to that tax year and one filed on or after January 15 applies to the next. Filing an appeal does not move the payment deadline. You may ask in writing, before December 31, to be billed on at least 80% of the protested value while the appeal is pending. Comparable market sales count as evidence, while forced, distressed and foreclosure sales are generally not.

sections.h2: What happens if the tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
The county moves from an execution notice to a notice of seizure, then to a public auction. If the bill is still unpaid 30 days after the execution notice, a notice of seizure goes out by certified, restricted delivery mail, and the property is advertised once a week for three consecutive weeks before the sale.

The owner, a grantee of the owner or a mortgage or judgment creditor may redeem within 12 months. Interest on the bid is 3% in months one to three, 6% in months four to six, 9% in months seven to nine and 12% in months ten to twelve. If nobody redeems, the Tax Collector issues a tax deed. The deed is not a warranty deed and conveys only the county's interest. A winning bidder who fails to pay is liable for $500 per property.

State law backs this up: 12-51-120 requires a certified mail notice to the owner between 45 and 20 days before redemption ends.

sections.h2: How are taxes handled when you sell a Spartanburg County house?
sections.html:
The unpaid balance, including any penalties, is normally settled at closing from the seller's proceeds. State law lets the county auditor apportion taxes when a property is transferred (12-45-140), so ask the closing attorney how the current year was split.

  • Pull the parcel's tax bill and any execution notice before you list or accept an offer.
  • Ask the Treasurer for a payoff amount that includes penalties.
  • If the bill went to the prior owner, ask about a penalty waiver under 12-45-180.
  • Tell any cash buyer upfront if the tax sale clock is running.

faqs.q: When are Spartanburg County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due between September 30 and January 15. A 3% penalty applies if unpaid by January 16, another 7% after the first days of February and another 5% by March 17, for a total of 15%.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Spartanburg County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 90 days from the date the Assessor mails the notice. Appeals must be in writing, and filing one does not extend the tax due date.

faqs.q: Can I get my Spartanburg County house back after a tax sale?
faqs.a: Yes, for 12 months after the sale. The defaulting owner, a grantee or a mortgage or judgment creditor can redeem by paying the taxes, penalties and costs plus 3%, 6%, 9% or 12% interest depending on the month.

faqs.q: Will the 15% reappraisal cap apply after I sell?
faqs.a: Not always. The cap does not apply to property that sold, had an assessable transfer or has new or improved structures. A buyer should expect a bill based on the new value.
